answer: Sybil resistance arises when each identity must finish a prescribed chain of modular squarings before receiving credit: within one chain, each result depends on the previous one, so GPUs cannot parallelize its steps. Clones can run as separate chains, but each requires its own sequential work, imposing a real time and hardware cost rather than making Sybil identities impossible. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently; karst, sable, and trellis can serve as domain-separation labels, not security guarantees.
